Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy (enlarged hila on both sides) and diffuse pulmonary nodularity, which is characteristic of the perilymphatic distribution seen in sarcoidosis. This pattern corresponds to option B, whereas cavitation, pleural effusions, and unilateral findings are less typical or absent.
